Short answer
- From your catalog memory the only named product I found is the "Harbor Task Lamp" — that’s a reasonable candidate to consider, but the catalog entry in memory contains no technical specs or provenance, so you must verify its energy and light-performance specs before buying.
- If you want general guidance to choose the most energy-efficient desk lamp for an office, follow the checklist and target specs below (I explain why each item matters and which claims you must verify).

Quick question before I go further
- Do you want a single lamp recommendation (style, budget, number of workstations), or a shortlist for purchasing several fixtures for an office? Any preference for color/finish, USB charging or clamp/base mount, or smart-home integration?

Why the Harbor Task Lamp is worth looking at (but needs verification)
- What I found in your saved catalog: an item called “Harbor Task Lamp” (plus category entries for adjustable/task lamps and lighting products).
- Evidence available: the catalog memory contains the product name but no extractors or provenance data (no wattage, lumen, efficacy, ENERGY STAR/DLC, CRI, color-temp, dimming, or warranty info).
- What to verify for Harbor Task Lamp: rated power (W), delivered lumens (lm), lumens per watt (lm/W), color temperature (K), CRI, dimmability, presence of occupancy sensor or auto-off, any ENERGY STAR or DLC listing, warranty and return policy, and mounting options.

Checklist of features and target specs for an energy-efficient office desk lamp (with why they matter)
- LED source (why): LEDs are far more efficient and longer-lived than incandescent or CFL. Claim to verify: lamp uses integrated LED or replaceable LED module.
- Efficacy: aim for >= 80 lm/W if listed; higher is better. Why: higher lm/W means more visible light per watt of electricity. Verify: published lumen output and wattage, then compute lm/W.
- Task-light output: 400–800 lumens for focused desk work depending on task and distance (400–500 lm for basic computer work; 700–800 lm for detailed paper tasks). Verify: listed delivered lumens.
- Color temperature: choose 3000–4000 K for office comfort (3000 K warm, 4000 K neutral/cool). Verify: product’s CCT (correlated color temperature).
- Color rendering (CRI): CRI ≥ 80 minimum; ≥ 90 preferred for color-critical tasks. Verify: CRI value on spec sheet.
- Dimmable control: saves energy and improves comfort. Verify: type of dimming (continuous, stepless) and compatibility with controls.
- Controls & automation: motion/occupancy sensors, timers, or daylight harvesting save energy in shared spaces. Verify: presence and sensor specs.
- Certifications: ENERGY STAR or DesignLights Consortium (DLC) listing is strong evidence of efficiency and performance. Verify: listing on ENERGY STAR/DLC databases or label on product.
- Warranty and rated life: look for 25,000–50,000 hours or longer and a multi-year warranty. Verify: rated lifetime and warranty terms.
- Glare control & distribution: directed, diffused, or shielded optics to prevent eye strain. Verify: beam angle, diffuser type, or pictures and user reviews.

How to evaluate a specific model (step-by-step)
1. Get the spec sheet or manufacturer product page. Confirm wattage (W) and delivered lumens (lm). Compute lm/W.
2. Check CCT and CRI values.
3. Look for ENERGY STAR or DLC listing (search those databases or ask vendor).
4. Confirm dimming/controls and any sensors.
5. Verify mounting type and adjustability to make sure it lights the work surface, not the eyes.
6. Compare price vs. expected energy savings and lifetime: estimate annual energy use (W × hours used per day × days) and compare to alternatives.
7. Check warranty and return policy.

Example energy calculation (how to compare quickly)
- Lamp A: 10 W, 600 lm → 60 lm/W
- Lamp B: 16 W, 1200 lm → 75 lm/W
If both give the same usable task light at the desk, Lamp B’s higher lumen output may be better for larger tasks, but Lamp A is more efficient per watt. Use delivered lumens and required task lumens to pick the minimally powered lamp that meets your needs.

Claims that must be verified before purchase (summary)
- Any numerical spec: wattage, lumens, lm/W, CCT, CRI, rated life hours.
- Any certification claims: ENERGY STAR, DLC — verify on the certifier’s site or label.
- Sensor/automation capability and its behavior (does it false-trigger, what timeout, does it integrate with building controls).
- Real-world performance: glare, adjustability, build quality — verify with reviews or in-person testing.

- Produce a short shortlist of well-reviewed ENERGY STAR LED desk lamps from the current market (I’ll need permission to look up live web info).
- Create a one-page spec comparison template you can use to evaluate candidate lamps.
